name: Human Rights
description: The long fight for equal rights: the end of slavery, votes for women, the civil rights movement, the end of apartheid and the struggles that go on today.

checkpoints.name: The first rights
checkpoints.note: Cyrus frees the captives in Babylon, Magna Carta limits an English king, and the American and French revolutions write down the rights of man; Olympe de Gouges asks for the rights of woman.

checkpoints.name: Ending slavery
checkpoints.note: Wollstonecraft argues for the rights of women and the first women's convention meets at Seneca Falls. Britain ends slavery in its empire, and the United States ends it after its Civil War.

checkpoints.name: Votes for women
checkpoints.note: New Zealand gives women the vote in 1893. Suffragettes campaign in Britain, and women win the vote in the United States in 1920 and in much of the world after the wars.

checkpoints.name: Civil rights
checkpoints.note: The United Nations declares universal human rights. In the United States, Rosa Parks, Martin Luther King Jr. and many others end legal segregation, and India and Africa win freedom from empire.

checkpoints.name: Freedom movements
checkpoints.note: The Stonewall riots start the gay rights movement, women campaign for equal pay and the right to choose, and Nelson Mandela walks free and ends apartheid in South Africa.

checkpoints.name: Rights today
checkpoints.note: Same-sex marriage becomes law in many countries, Malala speaks for girls' schooling, and Black Lives Matter and MeToo bring old injustices into the open.
